title: Building a hand that can do what ours can.
lead: A robot that cooks, cleans and uses tools needs hands as capable as ours. This is how far we have come, and where we are going next.

now.title: Step 1 of 5: the hand.
now.text: The first prototype works and the full hand is designed. Right now it is learning to grasp in simulation. Next, we build it for real.

chapters.title: The first hand
chapters.text: A 3D-printed thumb and index finger, moved by tendons the way your muscles move your fingers.
highlights: 8 joints, each moved by its own motor
Tendons cross every joint on its axis, so moving one joint never pulls another
Nothing moves until it is told to: safe from the first line of code

image.alt: The blue index finger and thumb of the prototype seen from a three-quarter angle.

chapters.title: A full hand, designed
chapters.text: Five fingers and 20 joints. The motors sit in the forearm, just like the muscles of a human arm.
highlights: 20 joints moved by 16 smart motors that know where they are
A small rigid bar bends each fingertip together with the middle joint, as in your own finger
Every tendon has its own channel through the palm and the wrist

image.alt: The white five-finger Tendra Hand V1 in simulation, palm forward, fingers slightly curled and the thumb swung out.

chapters.title: A digital twin
chapters.text: A simulated copy of the hand that behaves like the real one, so we can try ideas in minutes instead of days.
highlights: Physics for every joint and tendon
Copies your hand live from an ordinary webcam
Two arms with two hands: the first robot body

image.alt: Webcam teleop: an open, spread hand on the left, copied by the simulated five-finger hand on the right.

chapters.title: Learning to grasp
chapters.text: The hand teaches itself to pick things up, by trial and error, thousands of times over in simulation.
highlights: 77% of grasps succeeded after 49 minutes of practice
Training on cloud GPUs, with both arms
Now: calm, steady movements instead of shaky ones

image.alt: In simulation, a robot arm's white five-finger hand wraps around a red cylinder above a wooden table.

lessonsHead.title: Ideas we dropped, so you don't have to try them.
lessonsHead.lead: Every mistake is written down. Here are the ones that taught us the most.

lessons.why: Twenty-one motors needed a huge power supply and left no room in the forearm for the tendons.
lessons.lesson: Count the power and the space before you count the joints.

lessons.tried: Cheap motors that can't feel their position
lessons.why: Someone had to straighten the hand by hand before every start.
lessons.lesson: A motor that knows where it is is worth paying for.

lessons.tried: A tendon to bend the fingertip
lessons.why: Tendons stretch and go slack, and the fingertip has no motor of its own to pull the slack out.
lessons.lesson: When nothing can take up slack, use something stiff.

lessons.tried: Rewarding the AI for reaching the goal
lessons.why: It learned to hover just short of the goal, because reaching it ended the game and the points.
lessons.lesson: Check what your reward really pays for, not what you meant it to.

next.title: Build the full hand, and let it grasp for real.
next.text: After that come touch and sight, learned skills, and a robot that understands what you ask.
